rationale: This study examines community participation in community-based urban sanitation programs in Koja, Jakarta, using surveys (analyzed via exploratory factor analysis, cluster analysis, and binary logistic regression) alongside semi-structured stakeholder interviews, field observations, and educational outreach (mixed_methods). The primary mechanism family is participation_assistance, centered on community collaboration, socialization around drainage and treatment, and participatory community sanitation initiatives, while enforcement_sanctions is secondarily tested via the Sanitation Governance factor (policy enforcement and regular monitoring, which is statistically non-significant in the logistic model). The focal empirical outcome modeled in Hypotheses H1-H8 and Table 4 is citizens' willingness to participate in community-based sanitation programs, which represents an institutional/governance intermediate outcome (administrative_outcome) rather than direct physical connection or household service quality. Confidence is medium because exposures and outcomes are measured through cross-sectional perceptual factor scores and stated willingness to participate rather than evaluation of a specific statutory rule.
